rv.q: With its infectious energy and richly enjoyable performances, Kinky Boots feels like a show that has got legs.
Director/choreographer Jerry Mitchell marshals it all with smooth efficiency, and drives it with sexy, sassy class.
The musical makes Charlie seem less of a drip than he was in the movie.
And yet the whole thing canters along with engaging verve and vim, once a dull opening 15 minutes first quarter is done.
Kinky Boots – the Cyndi Lauper/Harvey Fierstein show which won 6 Tony Awards and pipped Matilda to the post as Best Musical of 2013 – compensates for that oversight, big-time.
Lauper has created a score that is as catchy and polished as the string of chart-toppers that launched her career in the Eighties.
But Kinky Boots is not the future of the musical.
He’s a sure-footed sensation, the clod-hopping show isn’t.
In summary, this show really doesn’t put a single stilettoed foot wrong.
Mitchell’s inventive direction and staging ensures that the show never stops moving and the dances are as high energy as Cyndi Lauper’s infectious tunes demand they be.

And, in this glorious feel-good musical by Harvey Fierstein (book) and Cyndi Lauper (music and lyrics), those boots are made for walking, talking, singing, flouncing and wearing well above the kneecap.

cn.t: Critics largely embrace Kinky Boots for its high-energy choreography and Cyndi Lauper's songs, though some find the feelgood formula thin. The West End production wins over skeptics, with Lola stealing the show while Charlie remains a weak center.
